key_insight: GPIC delivers a massively scaled (≈28 trillion pixels) image corpus that is permissively licensed, safety-filtered, deduplicated, and captioned by a state-of-the-art vision–language model—providing large, ready-to-use data splits (100M train / 200K val / 1M test) for visual generative modeling.
problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity of large, legally permissive, centrally hosted, and quality-controlled image datasets needed to train and evaluate scalable visual generative models.
method: Aggregate diverse internet images and standardize metadata; caption images using a state-of-the-art vision–language model.
Apply automated safety filtering and deduplication to improve data quality and reduce harmful/duplicative content.
Provide curated splits (100M train, 200K val, 1M test) and permissive licensing with centralized hosting for research and commercial use.
impact: Enables reproducible, large-scale training and benchmarking of image generation models without licensing uncertainty, accelerating both academic research and commercial development in generative vision.
visual_elements: Scale comparison bar chart: GPIC (28T pixels) vs. common datasets (ImageNet, LAION) to convey magnitude.
Pipeline diagram: data collection → VLM captioning → safety filter → deduplication → splits & hosting.
License & safety badges: icons showing permissive license, safety-filtered, and hosted accessibility.
Sample image grid with example captions and dataset split counters (train/val/test) to illustrate content and annotations.
paper_title: GPIC: A Giant Permissive Image Corpus for Visual Generation
paper_authors: Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran, Kyle Sargent, Suchir Agarwal, Michael Jang, Michael Poli
